description: Figure 26 is a composite of cellular-automaton (CA) simulation output maps — no plotted axes — arranged in two panels. (a) stacks three strain states (0.2, 0.23, 0.3), each row pairing a "Microstructure" grain map (left) with a "Dislocation density" colour map (right), every image carrying a 100 µm scale bar. Row headers read "DRX fraction(frist: 3.8%; total: 3.8%)", "DRX fraction(frist: 39.0%; total: 41.4%)" and "DRX fraction(frist: 57.7%; total: 98.1%)". Grains A, B and C are labelled in the first two rows. A bottom legend states "White grains: matrix, Green grains: first stage, Red grains: second stage". The shared colourbar is labelled "Dislocation density (×10¹³ m⁻²)" with ticks 4, 2.894, 1.805, 0.889 and 0.01; each density map is annotated with its range: ρ:1×10¹¹–1.529×10¹⁴ m⁻² (0.2), ρ:1×10¹¹–1.240×10¹⁴ m⁻² (0.23), ρ:1×10¹¹–2.984×10¹³ m⁻² (0.3). (b) is the constant 1050 °C case at 0.23 strain, "DRX fraction: 45.0%", ρ:1×10¹¹–3.067×10¹³ m⁻². Grain A remains orange/red (high dislocation density) in (a) at 0.23 strain while new DRX grains are dark blue; panel (b) is almost uniformly dark blue. The figure shows the increasing-temperature case reaches nearly the same total DRX fraction as the constant-temperature case, yet its matrix grains retain much higher dislocation density, which then drives rapid DRX growth.

subfigures.description: Three rows of paired CA simulation maps for the increasing-temperature case (950 °C → 1050 °C over strain 0.2–0.3 at 0.01 s⁻¹). Each row = left 'Microstructure' grain map, right 'Dislocation density' colour map, both with 100 µm scale bars. Row 1 (0.2 strain): mostly white matrix grains with a few small green grains, grains A, B, C labelled, DRX fraction(frist: 3.8%; total: 3.8%); dislocation map shows red/orange high-density interiors (grain A) and green/blue boundaries. Row 2 (0.23 strain): DRX fraction(frist: 39.0%; total: 41.4%), many green (first-stage) grains, grain A still orange-red with high density while DRX grains are dark blue; ρ range 1×10¹¹–1.240×10¹⁴ m⁻². Row 3 (0.3 strain): DRX fraction(frist: 57.7%; total: 98.1%), large red (second-stage) grains dominate; density map almost uniformly dark blue with faint green boundaries, ρ 1×10¹¹–2.984×10¹³ m⁻². Bottom legend: 'White grains: matrix Green grains: first stage Red grains: second stage'.

Constant-temperature reference at 1050 °C and 0.23 strain, 0.01 s⁻¹: left 'Microstructure' map headed 'DRX fraction: 45.0%', with grains rendered in many distinct colours (cyan, magenta, grey, dark red, blue, etc.) rather than the white/green/red staging scheme used in (a); grains A, B, C labelled; 100 µm scale bar. Right 'Dislocation density' map is almost uniformly dark blue (low density) with thin green grain boundaries, annotated ρ:1×10¹¹–3.067×10¹³ m⁻², 100 µm scale bar.

observations.observation: Panel (a) consists of three strain rows (0.2, 0.23, 0.3 strain) each pairing a 'Microstructure' grain map with a 'Dislocation density' map, and (b) shows only the 0.23 strain state at constant 1050 °C.
Printed DRX fractions in (a) are frist 3.8%/total 3.8% at 0.2 strain, frist 39.0%/total 41.4% at 0.23 strain, and frist 57.7%/total 98.1% at 0.3 strain (the spelling 'frist' is as printed).
The caption states (a) is the increasing temperature from 950 °C to 1050 °C in a strain range of 0.2–0.3 and (b) is the constant temperature of 1050 °C at 0.23 strain, both at 0.01 s⁻¹.
A shared colourbar labelled 'Dislocation density (×10¹³ m⁻²)' carries tick values 4, 2.894, 1.805, 0.889 and 0.01.
Colour-legend text at the bottom of (a): 'White grains: matrix', 'Green grains: first stage', 'Red grains: second stage'.
Panel (b) prints 'DRX fraction: 45.0%', higher than the 41.4% total printed for the equivalent 0.23 strain row of (a).

Annotated dislocation-density ranges are ρ:1×10¹¹–1.529×10¹⁴ m⁻² (0.2 strain), ρ:1×10¹¹–1.240×10¹⁴ m⁻² (0.23 strain) and ρ:1×10¹¹–2.984×10¹³ m⁻² (0.3 strain) in (a), and ρ:1×10¹¹–3.067×10¹³ m⁻² in (b).
In (a) at 0.23 strain, grain A is still rendered orange/red (high dislocation density) whereas the newly formed DRX grains appear dark blue (low density).
The dislocation-density map of (b) is nearly uniformly dark blue with thin green grain boundaries, i.e. low density throughout, unlike the heterogeneous (a) map at the same 0.23 strain.
Every microstructural and density image in both panels carries a 100 µm scale bar.
Grains labelled A, B and C are marked in the first two rows of (a) and again in (b).
The citing text states that the dislocation density of matrix grains A, B and C was still higher in the temperature-increasing case than under constant 1050 °C at 0.23 strain.

The citing text states that the disparity in dislocation density and the ongoing temperature rise promoted growth of first-stage DRX grains and nucleation in the second stage, raising the DRX fraction to nearly 1 at 0.3 strain.

In (b) the microstructure grains are drawn in many unrelated colours (cyan, magenta, grey, dark red, blue), a colour scheme not explained by the white/green/red legend of (a) and not defined in the visible caption text.
